newsitem.title: POLAND: Budapest, Prague bourses hit new highs this week.
newsitem.headline: Budapest, Prague bourses hit new highs this week.

text.p: An all-time high on the Budapest bourse and a 1996 record on the Prague exchange were the highlights on East European bourses this week.
The Central European Share Index (CESI) fell two percent this week to 1,508.77 after hitting a record on Monday. Zagreb gained but exchanges in Warsaw, Bulgaria, Bucharest, Bratislava fell.
BUDAPEST
The Budapest bourse was firmer this week and sharp rises by certain stocks pushed the BUX index to a new high on Monday.
The underlying trend remained bullish with strong corporate fundamentals, but analysts said investors were divided on the market's short-term outlook.

"(Domestic) small investors and speculators say that the shares are overvalued, while the institutional and foreign investors have a different opinion," said Tamas Revesz of Gog Securities, adding that the latter groups continued to buy.

All pharmaceutical stocks, home improvement products maker Graboplast and plastics firm Pannonplast hit new highs this week. Pannonplast last Friday announced the acquisition of Kaposplast, a step welcomed by analysts.
PRAGUE
The Prague Stock Exchange continued to post small gains this week, setting a new 1996 high on the PX50 index each day until Friday.

Late gains on Thursday by power company CEZ pushed the PX50 up to a 1996 high of 582.0, but the bourse fell on profit-taking on Friday, closing at 578.9, about 1.5 points higher than at Monday's open.
Dealers said that only blue chip issues were attracting interest in a fairly thin market, as investors were looking elsewhere in the region.
WARSAW
Polish shares fell this week but analysts expected the correction, caused by profit-taking after 11.6 percent growth since mid-August, to end by early next week.

Analysts said the crisis in the ruling left-wing coalition which followed the sacking of foreign trade minister Jacek Buchacz on Wednesday could slow expected growth next week, but was unlikely to halt it unless the coalition collapsed.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 2.6 percent from last Friday's close to 13,568.1 points.
Analysts also said that next week the bourse might be influenced by investors speculating before the release of companies' August earnings reports.
BRATISLAVA
Bratislava shares saw another week of listless trading as the quiet summer season wound down, with the SAX index falling gradually.
The 12-share index fell over the week to Friday's close of 212.56, from Monday's open at 221.79 points.
"Overall development at the bourse may be seen as unbalanced, and we expect the prevailing downward trend to continue over the next few weeks," said Jozef Cimra of ING Barings.
BUCHAREST
Shares traded mixed at the Bucharest bourse on Thursday, the week's second session, when turnover rose to 92.04 million lei, almost double the previous session's level.
Traders said they expected most prices to extend losses in the next few sessions as investors seemed to be in a profit-taking mood and sell orders were waiting to be matched.
BULGARIA
Only one stock -- Varna Grand Hotel -- traded on the Bulgarian stock market this week. The 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Index (RABSI) fell 41.07 points, or 0.24 percent, from last Thursday.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks traded mixed on Friday after firming through the week and were seen stable next week.
Some traders said increasing investor interest in food processor Podravka and confectioner Kras might propel their gains. But the much would depend on their later publication of 1995 financial data.
LJUBLJANA
In Ljubljana the SBI index fell 41.38 points, or 4.2 percent, to 941.04, and total turnover was at 372.5 million tolars.
Market participants said the index could fall further next week as investors moved their interest to shares of newly privatised companies.
TIRANA
Neither treasury bills nor state bonds changed hands during the two weekly sessions of the four-month-old Tirana Stock Exchange on Monday and Thursday. SEPT 05 CLOSE WEEK'S CHANGE 1996 HIGH 1996 LOW
